summary.short: FERC order under FPA section 206 instituting a proceeding against PJM Interconnection and its listed Transmission Owners on transmission service, cost recovery and interconnection for large loads. PJM and the Transmission Owners must show cause or propose Tariff revisions within 60 days. Issued June 18, 2026.
summary.long: Order under Federal Power Act section 206 instituting a proceeding in Docket No. EL26-67-000 against PJM Interconnection and its listed Transmission Owners. It makes preliminary findings that PJM's Tariff appears unjust and unreasonable for lacking provisions on large loads. It proposes a large-load definition: a new commercial or industrial customer at a single site with a peak load of 50 MW or greater, interconnecting above 69 kV, and not part of a co-location arrangement. Preliminary findings cover the study process and application process for transmission service on behalf of large loads, including a non-refundable application fee and readiness requirements; ongoing operational requirements such as telemetry, remote disconnection and ramp-rate rules; public posting of Network Upgrade cost data; a pro forma cost recovery agreement with minimum contribution and credit support; new transmission services for flexible large loads; evaluation of alternative transmission technologies; and generator interconnection processes for electrically proximate large load and co-located load. Within 60 days PJM and the Transmission Owners must either show cause or propose replacement Tariff changes. Within 30 days PJM must file an informational report on resource adequacy. Interventions are due within 21 days, and abeyance requests may cover up to 90 days. The refund effective date is the Federal Register publication date of the notice of initiation. The order states that it does not intrude on state retail authority.

notes: Part 1 of 2: covers the order from its caption through the ordering paragraphs; the appendix of commenters is in part 2 and not annotated here. Most findings are stated as preliminary ('appears to be unjust and unreasonable'), with PJM and Transmission Owners to show cause or propose Tariff revisions within 60 days. The registry metadata refers to parallel orders for other RTOs, but this text addresses PJM only. The order states it is limited to large loads not co-located with generation. The large load definition (50 MW or greater, above 69 kV, not co-located) is described as 'appears to be reasonable' and is not yet adopted. Relations and entities are limited to this part; the appendix may name additional parties. Part 2 of 2 covers the commenter and caption lists and the concurrences of Commissioners Swett, Rosner, See, Chang and LaCerte. Concurrences are not operative, so no obligations, thresholds or enforcement are coded here. Relation targets are not in the registry, so target_instrument_id is an empty string (the schema requires a string). The caption lists RTO and transmission owner respondents; only PJM is coded as an entity. Commenter names are not coded. Concurrences differ in how they describe the Commission's jurisdiction: Chang says the Commission does not pursue the broad jurisdictional assertion in the ANOPR, while LaCerte says the Commission has very broad jurisdiction over transmission. Footnote numbering in the extracted text is partly garbled. The schema requires section_status, but both relations and entities have entries; the not_applicable status below is set for schema compliance only.

enforcement.note: Part 2 of 2 contains only the service list and the concurrences of Commissioners Swett, Rosner, See, Chang and LaCerte, with footnotes. It has no operative provisions and no sanction regime. The LaCerte concurrence refers to possible Commission remedies and a 'deficient response' but states no sanction type, authority, penalty or cure period. Any enforcement provisions of the show cause orders are in part 1.
